newsitem.title: INDIA: Buoyant Indian shares meet with resistance.
newsitem.headline: Buoyant Indian shares meet with resistance.

text.p: India's bull market run slammed into a psychological resistance level on Monday as profit-taking set in after seven weeks of gains, traders said.
"We believe a correction is overdue," said R. Ramakrishnan, chief dealer at ASK Raymond James Securities Ltd. "The market is running into resistance at 4,400 levels."
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top-30 share index ended down 32.09 points, or 0.74 percent, at a provisional 4,291.73 -- after surging to 4,391.01 in the early trade.

A government decision at the weekend to divest holdings in four state-run firms -- Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL), Indian Oil Corp, Gas Authority of India Ltd and Container Corp of India Ltd -- was one reason for selective selling in some counters, traders said.
"The reaction in MTNL is a clear indication," said Antony Sequeira, managing director, at Arcadia Share and Stock Brokers Ltd.
MTNL shares fell 31.75 rupees, or 9.96 percent, to 287.0.
Analysts said the government decision at the weekend to raise 48 billion rupees ($1.34 billion) through divestment would discourage fresh position-building in these stocks.
In the case of MTNL, a divestment panel has called for the government to sell 47 million shares, and a fresh issue of 60 million shares. The government's holdings will then come down to 52.6 percent.
MTNL which has a monopoly on telephone services in Bombay and Delhi has already sold off 34.27 percent of its shares to the public.
The government has not set a price for the divestment of each stock but the market is more concerned over excess supply of shares, traders said.
Analysts expect the market to rebound after a technical correction propelled by rising inflows from foreign institutional investors (FIIs).
They see no slowdown in FII inflows which rose to $365.5 million in June -- the highest in 1997 -- from $198.4 million in May.

"Our markets are dependent on FII inflows," said Ramesh Damani, a member-broker at the BSE. "So long as the Dow Jones is doing well, I think we're going to see spill-overs into emerging markets like India."
But domestic investors were not fully convinced of a bull market, he said, adding that this might change when positive economic data becomes more visible.
"Software and pharmaceuticals are doing well," he said. "In other sectors, we'll see mergers and takeovers -- all these are good news for the market."
Leading software firm Infosys Technologies Ltd said on Monday its net profit soared 103 percent to 92.2 million rupees in the first quarter ended June 30.
Infosys shares leapt 181 rupees, or 9.03 percent, to 2,185 at the BSE.
